newsitem.title: USA: Entergy sees remaining power line back Sat.
newsitem.headline: Entergy sees remaining power line back Sat.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Tuesday that only one of its 500 kilovolt (kv) transmission lines was still out of service following a band of 20 tornadoes that struck Arkansas earlier this month.
"All towers are up, but they're still stringing the cable. It should be back in service Saturday," company spokeswoman Carol Copeland said.
All remaining transmission and distribution lines are back in service, she added.
About two weeks ago severe storms knocked out Entergy's five 500 kv transmission lines, six 161 kv lines and four 115 kv lines.
About 18,000 out of a total of 611,000 Entergy customers were initially without power.
New Orleans-based Entergy maintains about 119,000 miles of transmission and distribution lines in its service territory, which covers parts of Louisiana, Arkansas, Mississippi and eastern Texas.

Weather Services Corp is calling for more showers and thunderstorms in the area Tuesday, with gradual clearing expected Wednesday. Another wave of showers will likely arrive late Thursday and early Friday.
